worksheets.title: Parts of a Whole — Picture It

items.prompt: A chocolate bar has 6 equal pieces. Color 2 pieces. Write the fraction that shows how many pieces are colored.
items.hint: The number of colored pieces goes on top (numerator). The total pieces go on the bottom (denominator).

items.prompt: Look at the circle below divided into 8 equal slices. If 3 slices are shaded, what fraction is shaded?
items.hint: Count the shaded slices for the numerator and total slices for the denominator.

items.prompt: Draw a rectangle and divide it into 4 equal parts. Shade 1 part. What fraction did you shade?
items.hint: You shaded 1 out of 4 total parts.

items.prompt: A strip of paper is cut into 5 equal sections. 4 sections are red. Write the fraction that represents the red part.
items.hint: Red sections = numerator, total sections = denominator.

worksheets.title: Parts of a Whole — Story Problems

items.prompt: Zara baked a pie and cut it into 8 equal slices. She gave 3 slices to her neighbors. What fraction of the pie did she give away?
items.hint: Think: how many slices did she give (top) out of how many total (bottom)?

items.prompt: A class has 10 students. 4 of them are wearing blue shirts. What fraction of the class is wearing blue shirts?
items.hint: Students in blue shirts = numerator, total students = denominator.

items.prompt: Marcus has a garden divided into 6 equal sections. He plants tomatoes in 2 sections. What fraction of the garden has tomatoes?
items.hint: Tomato sections go on top, total sections go on bottom.

items.prompt: A box holds 12 crayons. 7 of them are broken. What fraction of the crayons are broken?
items.hint: Broken crayons = numerator, total crayons = denominator.

items.prompt: Two bars are the same length. Bar A is divided into 2 parts with 1 shaded. Bar B is divided into 4 parts. How many parts of Bar B must be shaded to match Bar A?
items.hint: 1/2 = ?/4. Multiply numerator and denominator by 2.

items.prompt: Fill in the blank to make an equivalent fraction: 1/3 = __/9
items.hint: Multiply both top and bottom of 1/3 by 3.

items.prompt: Which of these is equivalent to 2/4? Circle all that apply: 1/2, 3/6, 4/6, 4/8
items.hint: Simplify 2/4 by dividing by 2. Then check each option.

items.prompt: Fill in the blank: 3/4 = __/12
items.hint: Multiply numerator and denominator of 3/4 by 3.

items.prompt: Step 1: Write 1/2. Step 2: Multiply top and bottom by 3. Step 3: Write your new fraction.
items.hint: 1×3=3 and 2×3=6, so the answer is 3/6.

items.prompt: Is 4/10 equivalent to 2/5? Show your work: divide numerator and denominator of 4/10 by the same number.
items.hint: Divide both 4 and 10 by 2.

items.prompt: Find the missing number: 5/6 = 10/__
items.hint: 5 was multiplied by 2 to get 10, so multiply 6 by 2 as well.

items.prompt: Simplify 6/8 to its lowest terms.
items.hint: Divide both 6 and 8 by their greatest common factor, which is 2.

items.prompt: Plot 1/4 and 3/4 on a number line from 0 to 1. Which fraction is greater?
items.hint: The fraction further to the right on the number line is greater.

items.prompt: Use the benchmark 1/2 to decide: is 3/8 greater than or less than 1/2?
Two fraction bars of equal length: one shows 2/3 shaded, another shows 3/5 shaded. Which is greater?
items.hint: Convert to a common denominator of 15: 2/3 = 10/15, 3/5 = 9/15. So 2/3 > 3/5.

items.prompt: Order these from least to greatest: 1/2, 2/5, 7/10
Compare 3/4 and 5/8. Step 1: Find a common denominator. Step 2: Convert both fractions. Step 3: Compare.
items.hint: 3/4 = 6/8. Now compare 6/8 and 5/8. Since 6 > 5, we get 3/4 > 5/8.

items.prompt: Use the cross-multiplication method to compare 2/3 and 3/4. Multiply 2×4 and 3×3. Which product is larger?
items.hint: Cross multiply: left fraction numerator × right fraction denominator vs right fraction numerator × left fraction denominator.

items.prompt: Which is smaller: 7/12 or 5/8? Show your work using a common denominator.
Put these in order from greatest to least: 3/5, 7/10, 1/2
Calculate: 3/8 + 2/8. Remember: add only the numerators, keep the denominator.
items.hint: 3 + 2 = 5. Keep the denominator 8. Answer: 5/8.

items.prompt: Calculate: 5/9 + 1/9. Simplify your answer if possible.
items.hint: 5 + 1 = 6. Answer is 6/9. Simplify by dividing by 3: 2/3.

items.prompt: Jayla walked 2/6 of a mile to school and 3/6 of a mile to the park. How far did she walk in total?
items.hint: 2/6 + 3/6 = 5/6. Same denominator, just add the tops.

items.prompt: Calculate: 4/7 + 6/7. Convert your answer to a mixed number.
items.hint: 4 + 6 = 10. So 10/7. Since 10 > 7, divide: 10 ÷ 7 = 1 remainder 3. Answer: 1 and 3/7.

items.prompt: Theo finished 2/8 of his homework before dinner and 5/8 after dinner. What fraction of his homework is done?
items.hint: Both fractions have denominator 8. Add the numerators: 2 + 5 = 7.

items.prompt: A water tank is filled 3/10 in the morning and another 4/10 in the afternoon. How full is the tank now?
Two friends share a pizza divided into 12 slices. One ate 3/12, the other ate 4/12. What fraction did they eat together? How many slices is that?
items.hint: 3/12 + 4/12 = 7/12. Since each slice is 1/12 of the pizza, that's 7 slices.

items.prompt: Priya read 5/11 of a book on Saturday and 4/11 on Sunday. Did she finish the book? What fraction did she read in all?
items.answer: 9/11 — she did not finish the book
items.hint: 5/11 + 4/11 = 9/11. She still has 2/11 left.

items.prompt: A smoothie recipe uses 3 bananas for every 2 cups of milk. Write this as a ratio in three ways: using ':', using 'to', and as a fraction.
items.hint: Ratios can be written with a colon, the word 'to', or as a fraction.

items.prompt: A class has 12 boys and 15 girls. Step 1: Write the ratio of boys to girls. Step 2: Simplify it.
items.hint: 12:15. Divide both by 3: 4:5.

items.prompt: If the ratio of cats to dogs at a shelter is 2:5 and there are 10 dogs, how many cats are there?
items.hint: 2:5 = ?:10. Multiply both parts by 2: 4:10. So there are 4 cats.

items.prompt: Are the ratios 3:4 and 9:12 equivalent? Show your work.
items.hint: Divide 9 and 12 by their GCF (3) to get 3:4.

items.prompt: For every 2 apples in a fruit bowl there are 3 oranges. If there are 8 apples, how many oranges are there?
items.hint: 2:3 = 8:?. Multiply both sides by 4: 8:12.

items.prompt: A car travels 150 miles in 3 hours. What is the ratio of miles to hours? How far would it travel in 5 hours at the same speed?
items.answer: 50:1 (50 miles per hour); 250 miles in 5 hours
items.hint: 150 ÷ 3 = 50 miles per hour. 50 × 5 = 250 miles.

items.prompt: In a bag of mixed nuts, the ratio of almonds to cashews is 3:2. If there are 30 nuts total, how many are almonds?
items.hint: 3 + 2 = 5 parts total. 30 ÷ 5 = 6 nuts per part. Almonds = 3 × 6 = 18.

items.prompt: A lemonade stand mixes 1 cup of lemon juice with 4 cups of water. If they use 3 cups of lemon juice, how many cups of water do they need?
items.hint: 1:4 = 3:?. Multiply both by 3: 3:12.
